title: [P2/S5] Safe auto-roll, dynamic dice multipliers and opt-in event rotations
description:
## Dependency
Do **not** implement before #5 (atomic seeded game loop), #6 (saves/recovery) and #3 (encounter host contract). The feature may otherwise multiply energy costs or duplicate rewards.

## Gameplay
- [ ] Auto-roll supports bounded queue/session; user controls start/stop, remaining energy budget, desired multiplier, and pause reasons.
- [ ] Always stop/pause for raid, heist, choices, upgrades requiring a decision, insufficient energy, background/unfocused page, save error, or user cancel. Preserve one-roll-one-transaction invariant.
- [ ] Dynamic multiplier selector only from valid values [1,2,3,5] (and future configurable set); never silently increase spending. Modes: fixed, conserve, boost on target tiles **based on currently known info**; no false predictions of RNG.
- [ ] Fast roll/fast animations never change probabilistic outcomes or skip mandatory award processing; disable race-prone multiple roll requests.
- [ ] Optional event config JSON `{id,version,startUtc,endUtc,goal,scoreTable,rewards,claimWindow}`; typed canonical action stream `DiceRolled, TileResolved, BuildingUpgraded, HeistCompleted, RaidCompleted` updates parallel milestones without paying core reward twice.
- [ ] Start with ONE low-cost 48h `Skyline Sprint` event plus daily quests; add excavation/derby and seasonal cadence after retention checks.
- [ ] Offline schedule and one-claim-per-ID persistence. NPC-only standings explicitly labeled as simulations. Never market nonexistent live players.
- [ ] Non-coercive login rewards, reset grace and clear expiry. Avoid constant flash notifications or deceptive streak penalties.

## Acceptance
10k+ simulated rolls across stop/resume, duplicate input, saved restarts and event expiry produce no negative resource balances, doubled payouts, invalid multipliers or undesired auto spending. Manual mode remains clear and fun.

title: [P1/S4] Make Sunny Suburb's voxel construction and mobile gameplay genuinely tactile
description:
## Context
Child of #4. Do this after a tested core (#5) and save (#6), and parallel to #3 encounter integration only once host contract is stable.

## Existing
`web/src/components/VoxelScene.tsx` contains 32 colored tiles, a basic token, two tumbling unnumbered cubes, OrbitControls and stack-of-box building tiers. It reads Zustand directly. `web/src/App.tsx` shows one district, upgrade modal, and simple HUD.

## Scope
- [ ] Actual visible numbered/pipped dice consistent with precommitted result; avoid re-rolling in rendering.
- [ ] Tile-by-tile token hop and restrained board focus; correct quick/skip animations.
- [ ] Five distinctive Sunny Suburb building silhouettes with tier 0–4 changes; animated block assembly, hit/shield damage and repair.
- [ ] Original scenery: roads, landscaping, props, ambient NPCs using reused/instanced geometry and verified asset licences.
- [ ] Chunky toy-scale visuals and explicit token palette per `DESIGN.md`; use `InstancedMesh`/shared geometry where beneficial after profiling.
- [ ] 320/360/390/430px responsive layouts, safe-area padding, accessible close X, tap targets ≥44px, no intrusive toasts.
- [ ] Audio one-shot concurrency control, mute, reduced-motion. No repetitive sound loops.
- [ ] Measured frame-time and memory on Android Chrome device, degrade shadows/DPR if needed.

## Acceptance
User can complete the full Sunny Suburb construction loop, recognize tier progression without inspecting numbers, and roll/build comfortably on portrait mobile. Actual device/browser recordings and test notes attached. No UI blocks an interaction.

title: [P0/S2] Versioned browser saves, offline energy catch-up and interruption recovery
description:
## Parent
Child of #4; depends on #5 pure reducer and durable roll/encounter IDs.

## Verified gap
`web/src/store/gameStore.ts` is memory-only: any reload resets resources, district and position. The HTML WebView code uses `localStorage` but stores transient roll flags without resumable timers and has incomplete validation. Android Kotlin SharedPreferences are not browser saves.

## Scope
- [ ] Versioned `SaveV1` with schema validation, migration framework and corrupted-data recovery.
- [ ] Atomic snapshot or journal strategy for `coins, materials, energy, shields, tile, building tiers, quest/event progress, pending/processed encounter IDs`.
- [ ] Recover from refresh/background during dice animation or minigame WITHOUT granting rewards twice.
- [ ] Offline energy regeneration based on `lastEnergyRegenAt` timestamps and cap, using monotonic/clock-change-safe policy; do not create unbounded income from device clock manipulation.
- [ ] Save on authoritative completed transactions; throttle presentation-only state; handle storage errors visibly without crashes.
- [ ] Graceful reset/export/import for developer troubleshooting; stable Android WebView/Capacitor storage plan later.

## Acceptance
Roll → land → reward → build → save → reload reproduces the same progress. Interrupt at every turn/encounter phase; resume deterministically, no soft locks or duplicate claim. Automated test coverage for invalid/tampered saves, versions, clock jumps, offline cap and interrupted rewards.

## Implementation progress — 8 October 2026

A first code implementation is available in **draft stacked PR [#13](https://github.com/sp80808/blockbound/pull/13)**, targeting gameplay PR [#10](https://github.com/sp80808/blockbound/pull/10). It includes versioned validated browser checkpoints, a settled-state-only autosave adapter, offline and in-session energy catch-up, UTC streak-day handling, and six focused regression tests. The pure save protocol compiled under local strict TypeScript and its six Node tests passed.

**Not yet complete:** full React build and on-device QA were not run, no multi-tab conflict support, persistent online/cloud authority is out of scope, and interruption/reward idempotency needs browser integration tests. Do not close this issue or merge the draft PR until those checks and PR #10 branch reconciliation are complete. The Android WebView remains a different HTML implementation.

title: [P0/S1] Reproducible web build and pure deterministic 32-tile game core
description:
## Parent
Part of #4. **Start here.** No Lovable/Replit agent credits required for work on the canonical GitHub `web/` source.

## Verified source state (2026-10-08)
- `web/package.json` has Vite/React18/Three/R3F/Zustand but no lockfile or test/lint scripts.
- `web/src/store/gameStore.ts` embeds `Math.random()` and `setTimeout`, resolves rewards only on GO and `tile % 4 === 0`, starts with only one district.
- Full 32-tile typed mechanics exist in earlier `app/src/main/assets/www/index.html` and `app/src/main/java/com/example/blockbound/game/GameViewModel.kt` **but cannot be used as-is**; these are references with gameplay bugs and different runtimes.

## Scope
1. Establish reproducible install/build on an independent branch: checked-in `package-lock.json` (or one declared manager), compatible node engines, `npm run test`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint` where feasible; no expensive hosted CI required yet.
2. Extract `game/rules/` and `game/content/`: board tile table exactly 32 entries; seed-injected dice; turn lifecycle `READY→ROLL_COMMITTED→ANIMATING→RESOLVING→COMPLETE`.
3. Unique roll IDs; spend dice energy once; consistent multiplier bounds 1/2/3/5; stepwise traversals and correct passing/landing rewards.
4. Port tile types/materials/shields/energy/coin/mystery/encounter triggers; ensure all currency calculations integer, capped, validated.
5. Zustand as adapter over pure reducer; actual game outcome precommitted before any dice animation. Ensure turbo/skip affects only presentation.
6. Unit/property tests: dice valid 1..6; 32-index wrap; no double payout; roll denial at insufficient energy; every tile mapped; 10k seeded roll simulation for invariant checks.

## Acceptance
An offline session repeatedly rolls valid dice, visibly traverses 32 spaces, resolves each landing accurately and receives materials enabling an upgrade. No duplicate spending or payout from repeated tap/animation complete. Build + unit tests actually run; provide logs, not placeholders.

## Out of scope
No server, online ranks, real-player raids, monetization, or parallel app rewrite. Requires separate save PR (#6) for reload-proof state.

title: [P0] Consolidate Blockbound Web/R3F and Android WebView to one product source
description:
## Verified problem (8 October 2026)
The `web/` Vite + React 18 + R3F client and `app/src/main/assets/www/index.html` HTML/Three.js game **are different game implementations**. Android `MainActivity.kt` currently loads the HTML assets, not the generated Vite build. Kotlin/Compose code under `app/src/main/java/com/example/blockbound/` is an earlier reference implementation.

This divergence creates a serious integration risk: Web game has one district, blank dice cubes and simplified tile rewards, while the standalone WebView HTML has richer pipped dice, heists, raids, typed tile definitions, regeneration and localStorage.

## Work
- [ ] Reproducibly install/build `web/`: lockfile, npm test/typecheck/lint scripts and CI.
- [ ] Extract pure TS game core: 32 typed tiles, seeded dice and idempotent reward/economy reducer; port useful legacy rules with explicit parity fixtures.
- [ ] Implement real pipped 3D dice settlement, tile-by-tile token movement, offline regeneration and validated versioned saves.
- [ ] Choose one Android packaging path (Capacitor or generated asset WebView); ensure same Vite bundle powers Android and browser.
- [ ] Only then retire separate HTML game after verified feature parity and Android device checks.
- [ ] Add mobile portrait, safe areas, input gesture, WebGL context recovery and performance QA.

## Acceptance
One authoritative source `web/`: browser and Android deliver same tested gameplay, save/reload, character movement, rewards, raids/heists via host interface, build/repair visuals. No second economy fork; no Android-only duplicated HTML copy masquerading as synchronized output.

See [README](https://github.com/sp80808/blockbound/blob/main/README.md), [architecture](https://github.com/sp80808/blockbound/blob/main/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md), and [tech stack PR](https://github.com/sp80808/blockbound/pull/2).

title: [P1] Integrate isolated Vault Heist and Town Raid minigames from Lovable lab
description:
## Context
The canonical product is `web/` (React + TypeScript + Three.js / R3F / Zustand). The existing Android WebView `app/src/main/assets/www/index.html` contains heist/raid logic that is **not** ported to `web/`. The legacy implementation has potential repeated-claim/repeated-click bugs. Keep Android WebView and Kotlin code for reference only; do not implement a fourth full product.

## Sandbox & design handoff
- [Blockbound design and visual contract](https://github.com/sp80808/blockbound/blob/docs/parallel-minigame-handoff-20261008/DESIGN.md)
- [TypeScript integration contracts](https://github.com/sp80808/blockbound/blob/docs/parallel-minigame-handoff-20261008/TECHSTACK.md)
- [Docs PR #2](https://github.com/sp80808/blockbound/pull/2)
- [Lovable Minigames Lab](https://lovable.dev/projects/cf80f3fa-4225-4df0-916d-dc7567b1411a)

## Work
- [ ] Complete standalone Vault Heist: nine unique safes, three picks, precommitted deterministic rewards, original 3D presentation and once-only completion.
- [ ] Complete standalone Town Raid: three labeled NPC targets, selectable shield/hit fixture, physical voxel fragments, single target and once-only completion.
- [ ] Provide pure TypeScript reducers, typed v1 `EncounterPlan` / `EncounterResult`, and deterministic tests.
- [ ] Export lab code from **separate** repo/feature branch; no unreviewed write from Lovable into Blockbound's `main`.
- [ ] Add `INTEGRATION.md` and actual dependency/license inventory.
- [ ] Review source into `web/src/minigames/`; wire host tile `RAID`/`HEIST` through a new engine-owned encounter plan.
- [ ] Validate once-only coin/material rewards in host and event/quest hooks; minigame must not mutate global coins, saves or Zustand directly.
- [ ] Confirm browser refresh/close/re-entry safety and portrait mobile touch behavior; performance and reduced-motion check.

## Acceptance
A single 32-tile board landing launches the correct modal, playing it resolves a visually correct outcome once, one host transaction grants the expected reward, and player returns to the same board. Double clicks, invalid choices, cancellation, reload and repeated confirm cannot mint duplicate rewards. Backed by tests and a reviewed integration PR; no claims of multiplayer where only NPCs exist.

## Non-goals
No actual friend attacks, ranked leaderboards, auth, monetization or untrusted client-side competition without a server-authoritative backend.
